Method of Attack: The attackers leverage malicious Python packages to distribute the malware. They use polymorphic malware, reboot persistent and stenography to hide code inside packages, building a fake GitHub reputation in the process. After installing the malicious package, the setup.py script is executed, and additional Python packages are installed. The setup.py script downloads a .PNG image and saves it in the operating system’s temp directory. The setup.py script then uses the “Isb.reveal” function located in the malicious “judyb” package to extract a hidden code from the image downloaded.
Attack Vector: The malicious package is published on the Python Package Index (PyPI) under the guise of benign-looking packages, using typesquating attacks and uses homophones or typos to mislead developers into downloading.
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious “judyb” package on PyPI, use of a setup.py script that downloads a .PNG image and saves it in the operating system’s temp directory, use of the “Isb.reveal” function to extract a hidden code from the image downloaded.
